text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A large fire swept through a used clothing market in the industrial town of Zarqa; tens of stalls burnt along with a few cars parked alongside.
- The government decides on immediate cash compensation for farmers whose crops were damaged by the recent freeze.

- Karak governate starts early preparations for the coming November parliamentary elections; over 180 people declare their wish to stand as candidates in a backlash by many disappointed voters over the performance of existing deputies.
- Serious efforts underway to create a "democratic" party which includes leading opposition figures such as former prime ministers Ahmad Obediat and Taher Masri.
- Administrative and personnel changes in the ministry of education are expected in the coming few days.
- Leading Islamist deputy Abdullah Akaileh urges opposition to start Islamic-leftist coalition ahead of November elections.
